This article examines Indikator 1a, which tracks the proportion of newly diagnosed adults with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) who have undergone the relevant diagnostic investigation. Standardized diagnostic workups are critical for appropriate treatment planning, making this metric a key focus for the [[styregruppen-for-danibd|Styregruppen for DANIBD]].

Nationally, 79% of newly diagnosed adult IBD patients (1,887 out of 2,385) received the relevant investigation [^src1]. Regional performance varies, with Region Sjælland achieving the highest regional average at 86% (273/317), while the Capital Region (Hovedstaden) records the lowest at 76% (601/794) [^src1].

At the departmental level, there is substantial variation in clinical or registration practices. Among departments with larger patient cohorts, Randers Medicinsk Afdeling leads the country with a 94% compliance rate (81/86), followed closely by SUH Nykøbing F. Medicin at 91% (53/58) and HOL Holbæk Medicin at 90% (38/42) [^src1]. Other notable high-performing departments include [[nordsjaelland-kirurgisk-overafdeling|Nordsjælland Kirurgisk overafdeling]] at 88% (97/110) [^src1]. 

Conversely, several larger departments fall significantly below the national average. Hvidovre Gastroenheden trails with only 64% of patients investigated (164/256), followed by Gødstrup Medicinsk Afdeling at 65% (78/120) and Aarhus Lever-, Mave- og Tarmsygd. at 66% (98/149) [^src1]. [[slb-vejle-medicinsk-afdeling|SLB Vejle Medicinsk Afdeling]] also sits below the national average at 76% (71/94) [^src1].

Statistical outliers are heavily influenced by small sample sizes. [[rigshospitalet-med-klinik-mave-tarm-lever|Rigshospitalet Med. Klinik Mave-, Tarm- og Leversygd.]] reports the lowest absolute figure at 43% (3/7), while AAUH Thisted Medicinsk Afdeling reports 100% (3/3) [^src1]. Both departments have extremely wide 95% confidence intervals, indicating that these extremes are likely artifacts of low patient volumes rather than systemic failures or perfection. 

Because the provided data represents a single reporting period, no longitudinal trends regarding improvement or decline can be established. Furthermore, the source table does not define a specific target threshold or standard, meaning no formal met or missed targets can be evaluated.

Summary: Tabellen viser regionale og lokale resultater for Indikator 1a og afslører stor geografisk variation — fra 43 % ved Rigshospitalet til 100 % ved AAUH Thisted — hvilket indikerer betydelige forskelle i udredningspraksis eller registreringskultur på tværs af danske hospitalsafdelinger.
